raw_response:
I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation this year. That is what I know best in Quzhou County, and at my age I want a steady, familiar plan with work I can still manage and that machines can help with. The winter wheat is already the backbone of my land use, and after wheat harvest I will plant summer maize right away so the land does not sit idle. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I care more about stable yield and less trouble than saving seed myself. I will not make the management too aggressive: enough fertilizer to hold yield, several irrigations for wheat, fewer for maize if rain is normal, and pesticides only when needed so I do not waste money or add extra fieldwork. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing and fits the local machinery. My goal is not the highest possible yield. I want a dependable harvest, manageable labor, and lower risk.
